spans.s:
effigy, burning the
------------------------------------------
Burning the effigy of a person religiously (this is called ākṛtidahana) has been recommended by the धर्मशास्त्रस् in such cases where there is enough evidence to believe that he might have died and neither the body nor its parts were available for च्रेमतिओन्.
An effigy is prepared out of palāśa (Butea frondosa) stalks and leaves, 360 in number. These stalks are used in the prescribed manner such as 40 pieces for the head, 20 for the chest, 30 for the abdomen and so on. If he had kept the Vedic fires, then, his sacrificial vessels are also to be consigned to the fire as in a regular च्रेमतिओन् when the body is available.
In case the person were alive and returned, then, all the सṁस्कारस् or sacraments had to be repeated again including remarrying his own wife.
